result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the five colors should stay. Both flag Sage text as too low-contrast and suggest similar small additions, such as a hover rust and a second paper tone. A explains better why the palette works: it calls the rare rust accent what makes it feel deliberate, and it points to typography, spacing and small caps as the real sources of premium feel. B is more careful to label its contrast figures as estimates, but it adds more value-level tweaks and leaves the premium point to a single closing sentence. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep all five colors, flag that Sage is too faint for text, and add a few derived shades (a darker hover rust, a second paper tone) rather than new accents. B explains better why the palette works: keeping Rust rare is what makes it feel deliberate. It also points clearly to typography and spacing as the real source of a premium feel. A is a bit tighter, but it gives only one line on where premium comes from, and its list of tweaks is just as long.
